Source: https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Think-Aloud_Protocol_of_Instagram_Feed_and_Fitspiration_Browsing_/21195811 (file "Fitspiration Transcripts (concurrent & retrospective).docx"; Davies, Turner & Udell, University of Portsmouth, 2022)
Licence: CC BY 4.0
Description: Concurrent think-aloud responses of ~18 female participants (pseudonyms) scrolling a fixed set of 20 Instagram "fitspiration" posts, grouped per image, followed by retrospective think-aloud; same study as the feed file.

Fitspiration Transcripts (concurrent & retrospective)
All Participants

Participant 2
Fitspiration – Retrospective
R: Were there any posts that really stood out to you?
Rose: The yoga one [image seven] I think it was because it was so different to the other ones, the other ones were so incredibly posed but, in a way, to show your butt, show your legs, show your boobs and to show how beautiful you are. Whereas this one was purposely focussing on look at the pose I am doing, because this is a challenging pose and it can show you what you can do. And you can see that the woman, she wasn’t actually looking at the camera, she wasn’t engaging with the camera she was just trying to hold the pose which is difficult to hold and her outfit was there to be comfortable not to necessarily to show her assets and her hair. So, that was the one that kind of stood out to me.
R: Where there any posts that made you feel anything in particular?
Rose: I think it’s just, some of the posts, even like the last one here, it’s like I don’t know how the girls that post those pictures think that we can relate to it. It’s just so unrelatable because they put so much effort in a way to prepare for that shooting and then they just go out on the street like ‘yeah, this is me, this is how I look’ – no you probably spent an hour doing that and then you try to tell us that this is how you walk to Starbucks, in your gym clothing. So, I think that some of them need to take a little reality check and be like ‘what am I actually trying to promote?’.

Jamila: Yeah some of them because the scenery looked quite nice. Only one of them was properly mid exercise, all of the rest of them were like mirror selfies posing, which is a bit… I don’t really like the point in that sometimes.
R: Would you say that the one that was actually doing exercise, was that preferable?
Jamila: Yeah, I would probably prefer watching someone actually do their routines because you can actually learn from that and incorporate it into your own routines at the gym. The mirror selfies were just showing you their figure and they all pretty much had the same figure.
R: Why do you think that is?
Jamila: Probably because they see other people with that figure and they aim to look like the others, possibly because of influencing and ‘likes’ because they get more ‘likes’ because they have that certain body type and so they want that as well.
R: So, do you think that there is a certain body type on Instagram?
Jamila: For Instagram, yeah. There is a sort of body type for people that want to look like something, but most of the time there is a lot of range, but there is a specific body type that loads of girls want to have which is like the slim waist and stuff like that, but it’s not exactly ideal because then it is just teaching young people that they’ve got to look a certain way, which isn’t good.
R: So, do you think that accounts like these with this body type, would you say they are popular because of that?
Jamila: Yeah, they are probably popular because of the way the girls are looking, the shape they are.
R: Why do you think people might prefer that shape, what do you think has influenced that?
Jamila: I think they prefer that body shape because they think that other people prefer that and they think that because other people prefer it they should look like that because then they will get liked more.
R: Do you think that that sort of body shape gets quite a lot of air time then?
Jamila: Yeah, quite a lot.
R: Did any of them make you feel anything in particular?
Jamila: Not really. I liked some of the two pieces but they didn’t really affect.
R: That’s good. Did you find that you paid attention to some more than others?
Jamila: Yeah, probably.
R: What do you think…
Jamila: Um, some of them were just more visually interactive, some of them were just quite plain they were less interesting to look at. The outdoors ones because you could see all the scenery were just a bit more interesting to look at.
Participant 21
Fitspiration – Retrospective
R: Did any of those stand out to you in particular?
Lucy: I like this one [image twenty], I don’t know, she just looks really good, I think. And the one with the nice views I like as well [image fifteen], just because I would love to do that.
R: Did any of them make you feel anything in particular?
Lucy: I think a lot more motivated, they had very motivating like quotes on them, some of them.
R: Was it the words that made you feel motivated then, more than the images?
Lucy: I think a bit of both. But the words more so.
R: So, would you characterise that as either a positive or a negative effect?
Lucy: Positive I would say.
R: So, you mentioned that some of the gym selfies looked a bit fake.
Lucy: (laughs), just because the one above [image five] is really natural and she like laughing and then the one in the gym [image six], she was just like posing and it looked really fake.
R: So, did you have a preference then?
Lucy: Yeah, yeah, the more natural ones.
R: Do you think they have different impacts on people?
Lucy: Definitely the more natural ones, have a more positive affect.
R: What do you think was the difference between ones you liked more and one’s you didn’t like so much?
Lucy: I think again the ones that are really posed, trying to, I don’t know instead of trying to send a message I think they are just trying to show off their own figure. If you get what I mean. Obviously, they have the right to show off what they’ve got but I feel like when you’re proper posing for it that doesn’t show what you actually look like.
Participant 22
Fitspiration – Retrospective
R: Did any of those stand out to you in particular?
Maya: Probably I would say the one in the pink outfit, I liked her outfit so I would say it stood out a bit more. And there was one with quite a long caption, that one stood out because I wanted to read it because I was nosey at what she had to say.
R: Do you find you read longer captions more?
Maya: Yeah.
R: Why do you think that is?
Maya: I don’t know, I guess if I see more I’ll always click that and read it all, just curious I think.
R: So, did any of them make you feel anything in particular?
Maya: Not massively.
R: A little bit though?
Maya: A little bit, obviously because it was like all gym stuff like that.
R: What was that specifically that it made you feel?
Maya: I think it just makes you feel like you want to go out and do that sort of thing.
R: Do you think that’s positive or negative?
Maya: I’d say positive. Definitely motivating.
R: Did you find that you liked some more than others?
Maya: Yeah, I suppose so.
R: What would you say it was about some of them that made you like them a bit more?
Maya: Some of them sort of had like inspirational captions. The one at the end, her caption stood out a bit more makes you feel positive.
R: So, would you say that that made you like the post more?
Maya: Yeah.
R: What about the person in the image?
Maya: Yeah, a little bit.
R: In what way?
Maya: Just because the caption was quite uplifting, she was praising herself, yeah so it just made you feel like they are quite like a happy person I guess, like they’ve motivated themselves.
